extracted.intended_audience: early-career cancer researchers, postdoctoral fellows, physician-scientists, quantitative scientists, undergraduate/recent_graduate students seeking research training
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions of Damon Runyon Foundation award programs, their aims, target applicants, and program-specific expectations (mentorship, career stage, research focus, and continuation eligibility). Useful for applicants deciding which Damon Runyon award to pursue and understanding high-level selection priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon Fellowship Award — support for postdoctoral training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Damon Runyon Fellowship Award supports the training of the brightest postdoctoral scientists as they embark upon their research careers. This funding enables them to be mentored by established investigators in leading research laboratories across the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets postdoctoral trainees; emphasizes mentorship by established investigators and placement in leading research laboratories. Implicit evaluation criteria: candidate promise as a postdoc, quality of proposed training environment and mentor, and potential for long-term research career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon–St. Jude Pediatric Cancer Research Fellowship — pediatric focus, early career
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides funding to early career scientists conducting research with the potential to significantly impact the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of one or more pediatric cancers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target: early career researchers working on pediatric cancers. Key evaluative signals: relevance to pediatric cancer prevention/diagnosis/treatment and potential for significant impact. Joint organizational partnership (Damon Runyon–St. Jude) indicates emphasis on pediatric-clinical relevance and translational potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon Quantitative Biology Fellowship — quantitative/computational to biology transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to encourage quantitative scientists (mathematics, computer science, physics, engineering, and others) to pursue research careers in computational biology under the joint mentorship of leaders in both computational science (“dry lab”) and cancer biology (“wet lab”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key criteria: applicant has quantitative training and plans to transition into computational/cancer biology; project structured with joint mentorship from both computational and biological leaders. Implicit expectations: clear plan for interdisciplinary training, strong mentorship team bridging dry and wet labs, and research that leverages quantitative methods to advance cancer biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon–Rachleff Innovation Award — high-risk/high-reward without preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports exceptionally creative thinkers with “high-risk/high-reward” ideas that have the potential to significantly impact understanding of and/or approaches to prevention, diagnosis or treatment of cancer but lack sufficient preliminary data to obtain traditional funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit acceptance of projects lacking preliminary data; emphasis on novelty, boldness, and transformative potential. Programmatic feature: Rachleff Innovators are eligible to apply for Stage 2 Funding in the final year of their award. Evaluation will prioritize conceptual innovation and potential impact over preliminary results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award — support for early-career physician-scientists doing patient-oriented research
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports early career physician-scientists conducting patient-oriented research. The goal is to increase the number of physicians capable of moving seamlessly between the laboratory and the patient’s bedside in search of breakthrough treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets physician-scientists whose work bridges clinical and laboratory research; emphasis on patient-oriented/translational work and capacity to integrate bedside and bench. Programmatic feature: Clinical Investigators are eligible to apply for Continuation Grants in the final year of their award. Evaluation signals include clinical relevance, translational potential, and career trajectory toward physician-scientist roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon Physician-Scientist Training Award — protected research training for physicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports and encourages outstanding physicians to pursue cancer research careers by providing them with the opportunity for a protected research training experience under the mentorship of a highly qualified and gifted mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on physicians (MDs) seeking protected time for research training; key criteria include excellence as a physician, quality of the proposed mentor and training environment, and commitment to a cancer research career. Implicit expectation: structured mentoring plan and safeguarded research time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon–Dale F. Frey Award for Breakthrough Scientists — follow-on investment for exceptional fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: Select Damon Runyon Fellows and Damon Runyon Quantitative Biology Fellows who have greatly exceeded the Foundation’s highest expectations at the end of the Fellowship may be selected as recipients of the Damon Runyon–Dale F. Frey Award for Breakthrough Scientists to catapult their research careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded to a small number of exceptionally performing fellows; implicit criteria: outstanding research productivity/impact during the fellowship, exceptional promise for future breakthroughs. Purpose is additional investment to accelerate career trajectory; likely awarded based on evidence of exceptional achievement during the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damon Runyon Scholars Program (SPARK) — recruiting talented undergraduates/recent graduates
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensures that the best young college students and recent college graduates are encouraged to pursue rigorous scientific education and to commit their talents to tackling longstanding challenges in cancer research. Recognizes that emerging scientists will come from a variety of backgrounds; provides opportunity to pursue cancer research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target audience: college students and recent graduates with talent, passion, curiosity, and determination for cancer research. Explicit emphasis on outreach and inclusion of diverse backgrounds. Evaluation signals: demonstrated potential and commitment to research, and benefit from early exposure/rigorous training opportunities.
